# Reticle XR (reticlexr)

> Reticle XR is a high-level augmented reality (AR) SDK for React and Capacitor, published on npm as `reticlexr`. It lets web developers place GLB/GLTF 3D models on real-world surfaces in about ten lines of code: WebXR + Three.js rendering on Android with ARCore hit testing, plane detection, XRAnchors world-locking, tap-to-place, drag/pinch/twist gestures, runtime recolouring, model switching and screenshots, plus a native Capacitor plugin for ARCore session management on Android. MIT licensed, free, no per-seat pricing.

## Key facts

- Package: `reticlexr` on npm — install with `npm install reticlexr`
- Platforms: Android (Chrome WebXR + ARCore) in a Capacitor app, or plain WebXR in the browser; models render via WebXR — native model rendering is not implemented
- Stack: React, Capacitor, WebXR, ARCore, Three.js, TypeScript-friendly (ships its own types)
- Core APIs: `createARView`, `ARView.placeModel`, `moveModel`, `switchModel`, `setScale` / `rotateBy`, `setColor`, `takeScreenshot`, surface events, XRAnchor-backed placement that keeps models glued to real surfaces
- Use cases: product AR (furniture, appliances, retail try-before-you-buy), AR viewers, interactive 3D marketing, prototyping AR features inside existing React/Capacitor apps
- Documentation: https://reticlexr.vercel.app (root redirects to the getting-started guide)
- Live demo: https://reticlexr.vercel.app/demo — place, switch, recolour and photograph models in the browser
- Source code: https://github.com/ShahiCrafts/reticlexr (MIT)
- Author: Saugat Shahi (ShahiCrafts)

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/getting-started): Install reticlexr, wire it into a Capacitor app, and place your first model, then test on a real phone over HTTPS.
- [API reference](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/api): The complete public API of the SDK.
- [Compatibility](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/compatibility): Devices, browsers and platform support, with on-device test results.
- [WebXR vs native AR](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/concepts/webxr-vs-native): How the WebXR runtime compares with native ARCore, and what that means for placement and stability.
- [Architecture](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/concepts/architecture): How the SDK is layered — web runtime, React bindings, native plugin.
- [Gestures guide](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/gestures): Tap-to-place, drag to move, pinch to scale, twist to rotate.
- [React integration](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/react-integration): Using reticlexr from React components.
- [Model preloading and switching](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/model-preloading-and-switching): Preload GLB models and switch between them in place.
- [Colours and textures](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/colors-and-textures): Runtime recolouring and material customisation.
- [Overlays](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/overlays): DOM overlays in immersive AR sessions.
- [Screenshots](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/screenshots): Capturing AR photos from a session.
- [Troubleshooting](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/guides/troubleshooting): Common problems and fixes.
- [Known issues](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/known-issues): Current limitations, stated honestly.
- [Changelog](https://reticlexr.vercel.app/docs/changelog): Release history.
